title: Implement ODOC-231: ground lore's version control in git (committed citations, derived index, per-document history, branch/merge safety)
description: opum-agent decided this architecture under OPAG-204 (Accepted); opum-doc recorded it as ODOC-231 at docs/adr/ground-lore-version-control-in-git-with-committed-citations-and-a-derived-index.md (opum-doc repo), amended seven times same-day (ODOC-232/233/234/236/237/238/239). Git becomes lore's sole store of record for document history; the .lore/cache/snapshots/1 retention cache (cap 16, gitignored, machine-local) is replaced by small committed citations at .lore/snapshots/1/<kind>/<scope>/<name>.json naming a commit + verified projection_digest; queries are served by a gitignored, rebuildable SQLite index at .lore/cache/index.sqlite; generated files are regenerated in CI rather than merged; verified provenance becomes a required object (subject_digest/as_of/recorded_at). Per the ADR's own Downstream records: implementation sequencing is lore-cli's to plan, and lore-cli authors the ADR-0013 5th amendment (new committed .lore/snapshots/ member) plus a new ADR retiring the snapshot-retention spec (docs/specs/snapshot-change-and-provenance-workflows.md). LCLI-540, LCLI-474 and LCLI-539 are Done and satisfy specific narrow defects the ADR cites (edgeValue relation qualifiers; log.md merge-vs-replace; schema-export drift) but none of them implement this design. Verified absent at HEAD c40fa811 (2026-09-19): no .lore/snapshots/ committed, no lore history/diff/show commands, SNAPSHOT_RETENTION_LIMIT is still 16 (src/core/snapshot.ts:19), commands/snapshot.ts:77 still hardcodes maximum: 16, no SQLite index anywhere in src/. This task exists because OPAG-204's handoff asserted implementation was 'downstream and tracked' in lore-cli, and it was not until this filing.

(2) OPUM-WORKFLOW GUARD FALSE-ACCEPT (opum-fleet's defect, not lore-cli's - already reported to
opum-agent, recorded on OPAG-270, routed to opum-fleet). guard-trunk-writes.sh's tokenizer
(opum_git_trunk_violation in hooks/_lib.sh) resets its "start of command" flag only on a token
containing ; & | ( ) or a shell keyword - NEVER on a bare newline (word-splitting treats
newline as plain whitespace). So a multi-line Bash call like:
  git status --short
  git commit -m "x"
has its `git commit` become invisible to the guard even with no unrelated command first - two
consecutive git lines are enough. Confirmed live: a bare single-line `git commit` on dev IS
refused; the same commit as line 2+ of a multi-line call is NOT. This is how I committed
directly to dev this session (caught before push, recovered via branch+PR #185 - see this
task's description for the original command). Reproduction script (path may not survive - /tmp
is not durable - so the content is inlined here too):

  #!/bin/sh
  HOOKDIR=/Users/jdnewhouse/.claude/plugins/cache/opum-fleet/opum-workflow/0.9.0/hooks
  . "$HOOKDIR/_lib.sh"
  test_cmd() {
    label="$1"; cmd="$2"
    REASON=$(opum_git_trunk_violation "$cmd" "dev")
    RC=$?
    if [ $RC -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$REASON" ]; then echo "$label: REFUSED ($REASON)"
    else echo "$label: ALLOWED (miss)"; fi
  }
  VERB=commit
  test_cmd "A: bare git commit alone" "git $VERB -m x"
  test_cmd "E: git status newline git commit, no leading cd" "git status --short
  git $VERB -m x"

  (originally at /tmp/test_guard2.sh on this machine, this session - may be gone by now)

Nothing further needed from lore-cli here; opum-fleet owns the fix.

(3) OPAG-277 (lore Story -> Arc rename, execution task): no outstanding question from lore-cli.
Decision is closed (OPAG-255): rename to Arc, ratified, collision-checked clean against lore's

THE ONE THING A SUCCESSOR MUST NOT RE-DERIVE WRONG. LCLI-561 was routed as a FUTURE cost of this epic and is not. - Schema churn: the .lore/schemas tree was byte-identical across v0.6.0, v0.6.1, v0.6.2 and v0.7.0 (4bb5609a), changed at v0.8.0 (125934b1), and is 8 files on dev (700f1ed4). Three commits have ever touched it. A per-release VERSION stamp churns 21 files for nothing; a PROFILE DIGEST changes 2 of 5. LCLI-563 proposes the digest with the version carried only for the message, because prune is safe exactly when the tool can affirm the artifact is its own, and direction is not needed for that.
- This repository has NO .lore/profile.toml; the type vocabulary is src/core/profile.ts:1074. opum-cli-e2e's greppable OPAG-353 safe-condition INVERTS here -- an absent file reads as safe and is not. lore-cli is a generator, so the unsafe state is permanent rather than occasional. opum-agent has since written this into OPAG-354 as the strongest form of the case for LCLI-563: if the stamp is ever deferred because the operating rule covers most cases, that reasoning is wrong in the one case that matters.
- lore check on a workstation is NOT the gate. CI runs "bun run lore check" FROM SOURCE and ci.yml says so. The installed published 0.8.0 exits 6 on a clean dev because dev carries the unreleased Arc type. NEVER run "lore schema export" with the installed binary here: it would prune arc.schema.json and revert LCLI-554.
- LCLI-551 is a move plus a split plus additions, not a greenfield add. stale_after already ships as a TOP-LEVEL SIBLING property in 8 schemas; verified is an anyOf of {by, at} with both required and additionalProperties OPEN; subject_digest exists nowhere.

THE DESTRUCTIVE EXPORT IS AUTOMATED IN THIS REPOSITORY, NOT A HAZARD SOMEONE MIGHT WALK INTO. Found 2026-09-20 in my own working tree, at the end of the session, by reading git status before a commit rather than by any check.

WHAT I FOUND: "D .lore/schemas/arc.schema.json" and "M .lore/schemas/story.schema.json", unstaged, after a routine Quest write. arc.schema.json had been PRUNED -- the exact destructive outcome OPAG-353 tells sessions to avoid by hand.

THE MECHANISM, read from opum-workflow 0.10.0 hooks/sync-lore-after-tracker-write.sh:
- line 86 resolves the binary with "command -v lore", i.e. the INSTALLED published 0.8.0 on PATH, never "bun run lore" from source
- it then runs "lore check", which in this repository exits 6 with schema-drift findings, because dev carries the unreleased Arc type and 0.8.0 has no arc type
- line 161: because the exit-6 findings ARE drift, the hook runs "lore sync --json" to "repair" them
- 0.8.0's sync regenerates from a profile with no Arc, so it deletes arc.schema.json and rewrites story.schema.json

So the hook performs, unattended, the action an operating rule asks a human not to perform. FREQUENCY IS NOT ESTABLISHED: I observed the damage ONCE, and the very next --add-note on this same task did NOT reproduce it (only the tracker file changed). So "it fires on every tracker write" is NOT a claim I can make -- one occurrence and one non-occurrence is what I measured. The trigger condition is unknown; candidates include the hook keying on a STATUS write rather than any write, a bound/timeout path that silently skips, or lore sync finding nothing to change on the second pass. Whoever picks this up should establish the trigger before asserting a rate. There is no judgement step for OPAG-353's rule to attach to. This is the sharpest available argument for LCLI-563: a stamp the tool can read is the only remedy that reaches an unattended writer.

NOTHING SHIPPED, and the reason is luck-adjacent rather than a control. origin/dev and origin/main both carry 8 schemas with arc present, and no commit in 4c225010..origin/dev touches .lore/schemas at all. That held only because every commit this session staged explicit paths. "git add -A" stages a deletion for a merely-absent tracked file and then reports the tree clean, so it would have shipped a reverted LCLI-554 silently, inside a commit whose message said it was filing tracker records.

WHAT A SUCCESSOR MUST DO: run "git status" before every commit in this repository and expect these two paths to be dirty after any Quest write. Restore with "git restore --source=HEAD -- .lore/schemas/". Never stage them, and never use "git add -A" here. This is opum-fleet's defect to fix (they own opum-workflow); it is reported, not patched locally.

Follow-up on the destructive-export finding in opum-workflow's sync hook (reported from this record, routed via opum-agent): opum-fleet fixed and shipped it as opum-workflow 0.10.2, opum-ai/opum-fleet#209, tracked their side as OFLE-111. Their root cause matches the report -- opum_shrunk_files and opum_sync_files_changed were both keyed off 'lore sync --json's data.files[], which lists what the sync WROTE and never what it deleted, so it was structurally blind to a prune no matter how good the shrink detection was. The fix snapshots 'git ls-files --deleted' before and after the sync and diffs git ground truth independently of lore's own report, with a regression test whose stub sync deletes one file while reporting an unrelated one. They deliberately did not touch the PATH-resolution root cause at line 86 ('command -v lore'), on the grounds that from-source-vs-installed resolution is this repository's convention to own rather than something a generic hook should special-case. That is the correct call and needs no argument from here; it is the same substance as the local rule that 'lore check' must be run as 'bun run lore check'.

THE OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT HALF FOR THIS REPOSITORY: a restart does not fix it. 0.10.2 is not in the cache, so a restart rebinds to 0.10.0 as the newest present version and the exposure persists looking freshly current. Anyone picking up work here should assume the pre-fix hook is live until the plugin cache actually carries 0.10.2 -- verified by content ('ls-files --deleted' and 'git restore --source' present in hooks/sync-lore-after-tracker-write.sh), never by the directory name. This repository has already had .lore/schemas/*.json deleted by that hook once, so the standing mitigation until then is unchanged: read 'git status' before committing after any tracker write, and do not stage a schema deletion you did not intend.

Two limits on the claim, stated so a later reader does not overextend it. PID-to-session attribution is mine for 2 of 10 and inferred from socket numbers; the roster is not resolved and should not be quoted from this note. And I have not established whether .in_use is written at session start or refreshed, so a stale PID from an exited session would inflate the count -- which weakens the roster reading but not the 'no session is on 0.10.2' conclusion, since that rests on 0.10.2 being absent from the cache rather than on the count.

THE SIGNATURE TO USE IS opum_new_deletions, not either literal I originally named. It is a unique function name, present in both files, absent in 0.10.0, and carries no prose-collision risk. 'git restore --source' lives only inside a message body a future reword breaks silently; 'ls-files --deleted' is invisible to any check scoped to the hook file. Grep hooks/ as a directory in either case.

HOW IT GOT IN, because the how is the transferable part. The previous note's own sentence -- 'verified by content ... never by the directory name' -- was right about the method and wrong about the object, naming one file where the fix spans two. opum-agent independently hit the mirror image of the same error: measuring that one file and reporting 'ls-files --deleted DOES NOT EXIST IN THE SHIPPED FIX', which would have made a check reject 0.10.2 forever. Two sessions, opposite directions, one afternoon, on a message whose subject WAS this defect class -- the fleet block's 'name the object you measured and the object your claim is about' failing on a paragraph about itself. Object measured: one hook file. Object claimed: the shipped fix. They differ by hooks/_lib.sh. Corrected to opum-agent the same turn; its OPAG-341 check should key on opum_new_deletions.
